parsed.use_case: Operating systems and embedded devices often need to count active flags in a status or capability word to decide how many resources are enabled. The same count is useful when analyzing binary identifiers or masks.
system_examples: Linux kernel — counts enabled flags in bitmasks used for CPU capabilities, resource sets, and other low-level state.
Networking equipment — counts set bits in subnet masks to determine prefix length and address capacity.
parsed.explanation: A bit-counting routine processes the integer’s set bits or its fixed-width representation in O(w) time, where w is the number of bits; straightforward per-bit checking is also O(w), while repeated clearing of the lowest set bit takes O(k) for k set bits. This is a useful primitive in systems code, though as a standalone algorithm problem it is mostly a teaching exercise.
